Priya Patel: PRD intake — customer-driven prioritization request from GiantRetail (CUST-338).
Pri: Problem statement: GiantRetail needs per-customer quality thresholds on generated content so they can tune hallucination tolerance per route. Right now we have a global quality gate; they want different sensitivity for product-descriptions vs. legal copy.

Pri: Goals (what success looks like):
- Expose per-customer (and per-route) threshold config via API + Console (read/write via RBAC)
- Enforce thresholds in routing layer with automatic fallback to safer model variant when threshold fails
- Emit metrics and alerts: per-customer pass/fail, pct of fallbacks, and cost delta
- Pilot with 3 customers (incl. GiantRetail) and measure adoption & incidents

Pri: Non-goals:
- Not implementing per-prompt thresholds in v1
- Not changing model weights or retraining; only routing/filters
- No customer-facing UI for editing policies in v1 (console read + API write only)

Pri: Success metrics:
- Pilot adoption: 3 customers onboarded in first 8 weeks
- Operational: <1% increase in p99 latency for affected routes; fallbacks <5% after tuning
- Business: reduce reported hallucination incidents by >40% for pilot customers

Pri: Acceptance criteria (draft):
- API: create/update/get/delete per-customer threshold config (schema documented)
- Console: read-only view and link to API docs
- Runtime: routing honors threshold decisions and triggers configured fallback model
- Observability: dashboards with per-customer metrics and alert rule examples
- Tests: integration test that simulates failing threshold -> fallback

Pri: Edge cases to call out:
- Customer sets threshold so strict most requests fall back -> need safe default and quota protections
- Multiple thresholds (route + customer) conflict -> define precedence (route > customer > org)
- Backwards compatibility: existing routes without config should default to global behavior
- Data residency: threshold decisions must not leak customer IDs to shared logs (masking required)

Alex Chen: Quick clarifying Qs: do we need the eval harness to produce per-customer reference sets for automated tuning? Also who owns the privacy/compliance review for storing per-customer configs? @security?

Jamir O'Neill: I can take the technical spec for runtime changes. Proposed phased approach:
1) API + config store + docs (no runtime enforcement) — get early customer feedback
2) Runtime check + fallback policy in canary mode (metric-only) — iterate
3) Full enforcement with RBAC + quotas
Edge-case notes: ensure circuit-breaker if fallback model capacity is exhausted.

Maria Gomez: +1 to phased rollout. Non-goal reminder: do not build full UI in phase 1. Also can we default to an "auto" mode where we suggest thresholds based on historical evals? (opt-in)

release-bot: Reminder: next stable release window Apr 12-16. Any feature targeting enforcement in runtime should enter freeze by Apr 1. :calendar:

Priya Patel: Thanks. Plan: Alex to draft PRD doc and link it here, Jamir to own runtime design, Maria to own pilot onboarding details. Sync tomorrow 10:00am PST to settle scope. @Alex Chen please add acceptance-test checklist and a rough cost estimate (tokens & fallback model impact). :thumbsup:

Alex Chen: Will do — I'll push a draft PRD link by EOD and include an initial cost delta table.

Jamir O'Neill: I'll stub the spec and include edge-case playbook. Meeting invite sent for 10:00am PST.
